summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Nuclear endosperm (free-nuclear divisions without cytokinesis, e.g. Coconut water), Cellular endosperm (immediate cytokinesis, e.g. Datura, Coconut meat), and Helobial endosperm (intermediate, monocots).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
COCONUT ENDOSPERM ANATOMY
                        
   Liquid Endosperm (Coconut Water) ──► Free Nuclear Endosperm (Thousands of nuclei)
   White Kernel (Coconut Meat)      ──► Cellular Endosperm (Multicellular tissue)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Endosperm development always precedes embryo development to ensure a nutritional reserve for the emerging proembryo.

```
                            ENDOSPERM TYPES
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
  NUCLEAR ENDOSPERM         CELLULAR ENDOSPERM         HELOBIAL ENDOSPERM
  Primary PEN undergoes     PEN division is            Intermediate type;
  free-nuclear divisions.   accompanied by immediate   1st division forms 2 cells;
  *Most common type*        wall formation.            subsequent free nuclear.
  (Coconut Water)           (Datura, Petunia)          (Monocots)
```

### 7.1 Endosperm Developmental Types

1. **Nuclear Endosperm (Free-Nuclear Endosperm)**:
   - Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) undergoes repeated free-nuclear mitotic divisions without cytokinesis, creating a multinucleated central cell with a large central vacuole.
   - Cell wall formation occurs later from the periphery inward.
   - **Most common type** ($56\%$ of angiosperm families).
   - *Examples*: Maize, Wheat, Rice, Cotton, Coconut.
2. **Cellular Endosperm**:
   - Every nuclear division of the PEN is immediately followed by cytokinesis (cell wall formation), creating a multicellular tissue from the outset.
   - *Examples*: *Datura, Petunia, Utricularia, Balsam*.
3. **Helobial Endosperm**:
   - Intermediate type common in Monocot Order Helobiales.
   - First PEN division is accompanied by wall formation, dividing the embryo sac into a large micropylar chamber and a small chalazal chamber. Subsequent divisions in the micropylar chamber remain free-nuclear.
   - *Examples*: *Asphodelus, Saxifraga*.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Ruminate Endosperm
conceptBreakdown.title: Ruminate Endosperm
conceptBreakdown.content: In certain plant families (Annonaceae, Myristicaceae - Nutmeg, Betel nut), the endosperm becomes irregularly folded, convoluted, or chewed-up in appearance due to ingrowths of the seed coat, termed Ruminate Endosperm.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Xenia and Metaxenia
conceptBreakdown.title: Xenia and Metaxenia
conceptBreakdown.content: Xenia describes the direct phenotypic effect of pollen parent genes on the endosperm tissue (e.g., kernel color in maize). Metaxenia describes pollen genetic effects on maternal seed coats or pericarp tissues (e.g., date palm fruit maturation).
